messages.author: 51ea28fc190ac537
messages.subject: Rattle 2.5.26 released - new score options
parts:
Rattle has been updated to CRAN: 

  http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/rattle/index.html 

Changes include: 

  * Cross Tab option to Explore tab to generate cross tabulations of
    each categoric variable by the target variable. (Luke Lake)

  * Bug fix - improve how we obtain the plot number from the title,
    particularly in the context of translations.
  
  * Further translation markup.

  * Clean up the use of dfedit to edit a dataset and to score data interactively.
  
  * Minor improvement to spacing in Log tab.

 *  Start using the RGtk2DfEdit for the View and Edit buttons of the Data
    tab, and the Enter/Score option of the Evaluate tab. RGtk2DfEdit
    provides a spreadhseet like interface to the data. Various data
    editing options are available. Also press = to run an arbitrary R
    command on selected data (e.g. select two columns of data and issue
    the plot command).

Regards,
Graham

messages.author: 3a21f9c070d1a7a5
messages.subject: SV: Rattle 2.5.26 released - new score options
parts:
Hi all,

 

I wonder if it possible to use a Stop-Loss in R?

 

What I mean is if I want to do a prediction of a stock not only 10 days in the future but also the possibility to close the trade in for example 5 days if the price goes down 2%.

 

To clearify what I mean:

 

I put a lot of data in including the price of a stock into Rattle. I use a model to predict 10 days into the future. This gives a prediction without considering the price development during those 10 days. If I want to have close of position if the stock goes down for example 2 % how do I do that? Is it possible somehow to build this into the evaluation in R/Rattle?

 

Regards

Rolf
